properties.name: Mexico (earthquake coverage, coarse country outline)
properties.source_quote: issued three catastrophe (cat) bonds that finance $420 million of insurance coverage for the Government of Mexico against named storm events along the Atlantic coast of Mexico and earthquake events.
properties.secondary_source_quote: the World Bank issued 4 catastrophe (cat) bonds that provide the Government of Mexico with $295 million financial protection against earthquakes and $300 million against named storms.
properties.geometry_note: Simplified Mexico country outline (d). Vertex coordinates come from the public simplified country boundary at geometry_source_url (a commonly used public GeoJSON of Mexico), not from the prospectus. The World Bank press release and case study identify the coverage as being for Mexico / the Government of Mexico against earthquake events; they do not publish a polygon or any other region description beyond Mexico. This outline is not a contractual coverage area and not a contractual coverage box. Those deal geometries are not published on this site.
properties.note: Outline is a simplified Mexico country outline for display, not the bond's contractual covered area. Contract tests are not shown publicly.
properties.public_basis: World Bank press release, 17 April 2024, and World Bank case study, 27 February 2025: coverage for the Government of Mexico against earthquake events. Geometry is a simplified country outline (d), not a contractual coverage area or box.

name.citation: Short public display name assembled from published facts: IBRD and its “capital at risk” notes program (press release, 17 April 2024); Mexico and the 2024 issuance (same press release); “Class A: Earthquake event” (press fact sheet); and the prospectus cover title “Class A Floating Rate Catastrophe-Linked Capital at Risk Notes due April 24, 2028”. This display name is not itself a prospectus-defined title.

issue_size.citation: World Bank press release, 17 April 2024, fact sheet, Size (Aggregate Nominal Amount): “Class A: $225 million” under the heading “US $420 million catastrophe bond”. The prospectus cover (3 April 2024) states the same amount as US$225,000,000.

scheduled_maturity.citation: World Bank press release, 17 April 2024, fact sheet: “Scheduled Maturity Date — April 24, 2028”. The prospectus cover (3 April 2024) states “due April 24, 2028”.

trigger.citation: World Bank press release, 17 April 2024, fact sheet: “Trigger Type — Parametric, Per Occurrence”; body: “payouts triggered if an earthquake or named storm event meets the parametric criteria for location and severity set forth in the bond terms”. The press release and the prospectus cover do not name depth, magnitude, or USGS in that trigger description, so those words are not added here.

status.citation: World Bank press release, 17 April 2024: IBRD “issued three catastrophe (cat) bonds” that “attracted 27 institutional investors from around the world”. Public status label is “publicly issued cat bond”.

properties.note: Display approximation, not contractual coverage. A storm track entering this outline is a watch condition, not a payout.

tc_relevance.reason: A public source reports the outcome: World Bank press release, 7 November 2025, says the third-party calculation agent “concluded that Hurricane Melissa reached pre-agreed parametric triggers qualifying for a full redemption of the World Bank Catastrophe Bond”. This tool did not compute that outcome; the track checks in storms.json are watch conditions against a coarse outline only.
